The game is interesting as a light-weight take on a Civilization style game, but also an interesting experiment in use of AI. There's appeal in AI enabling a single (or small) dev-team to produce a small game at a cheap price. Maybe cheaply made is fine, if it's a cheap, and decent game. Well, that's the issue. It's not a cheap game. This is before getting into the separate debate about AI-ethics and artistic labor: AI is used to produce a game more cheaply here, but ultimately it's release price is 14-16 ish Euro/GBP/Dollars. That's just ridiculous. On top of that, the “surprise 1.0” release is undercooked: [list] [*]Game lacks any graphics settings except resolution [*]No keybind settings and generally few hotkeys [*] The game is also a CPU-hog, even when idle on a turn (given how simple it is, it has no business using so much CPU in relatively idle game situations: it'll jog your CPU as much as civ6 on a large map midgame save). [/list]

总的来说游戏的核心玩法还是挺有意思的，但是目前内容还有些空，相比特价的有口皆碑的精品游戏，买这个游戏我还是很后悔的，以下是我的槽点： 1、友善ai是没有的，没有势力之间的外交只有战争 2、海上单位是鸡肋又无敌的，鸡肋在于地图形状固定，只能绕着圈子走还不一定ai刷在海边，无敌在于ai不会出海上单位，只要你在海上溜一圈视野有了，海上刷的遗物拿到手软的。工人单位也是令人无语的，地块优化都是靠卡牌这东西不知道咋用，就一个采集，我又怕像”狩猎“卡牌一样永久删除地块资源而不敢用，感觉挺鸡肋。 3、地图编辑是没有的，地形固定只有一种形状的地图，无法自由更改地图形状和资源丰富度设定。 4、ai势力是单薄的，只有野蛮人可以打，没有其他单位和势力，这点可能也是造成第一个槽点的主要原因。 5、ai爆兵是无法理解的，围剿对面的营地结果突然在边上出来个兵 6、部分兵种是要先固定在攻击，你这个火炮榴弹炮我还能说是年代太早要瞄准半天，你个火箭炮凭什么和火炮这种老古董瞄准一样长的时间啊.....现在的军队都讲究机不可失，讲的就是要快速反应，等你固定好了对面ai都围剿死你了也太不合理了。 7、兵种射程问题，为什么弓箭、弩箭、火枪、狙击、游骑兵这种远程兵种都是两格的啊，这合理吗。兰斯导弹还行，毕竟核弹打下来是个范围伤害，射程很满意比其他的远多了。这飞机也离谱，二战你拿半自动都不一定打下来的飞机，火枪野蛮人给我飞机打下来了，我都信息时代打个中世纪应该是碾压才对，结果有的时候一下还杀不死。 8、部分机制解释不清，比如奇观“疗养胜地”，卡牌“每回合单位恢复4滴血，在每个城市范围内的未开发森林“，这是机器翻译的吗，意思是兵必须放在特定地块才能回血吗，还是说卡牌建造的位置？用下来实际情况好像是二者都必须满足，但是建设过程有的森林不知道为什么不能建可能是bug可能是我看错了。还有飞机的起飞具体解释鼠标放在上面是没有的。骑士的晋升兵种没有翻译。兵种之间的晋升关系也是两眼一抹黑，啥也不知道只能自己慢慢摸索，还有很多很多的解释问题不一一列举了。 9、优化问题，玩到后面资源起来有的回合一次给很多资源手牌，电脑就会卡，手牌多起来放置建筑就会卡住必须退到主菜单才能恢复正常。 如果说能添加内容和更多玩法，改善优化，其他的小问题不改善，我也愿意好评，目前的游戏内容玩了一遍没有第二遍体验的欲望

Sadly, while the gameplay loop is moderately fun, that's about the end of the "good". The Barbarians (the main and I guess only enemy) always seem to be ahead of you on tech no matter what you do. Have fun fighting tanks with swordsmen. The game also uses emojis for in-game icons almost as if it were designed to be a mobile game which detracts a lot from the experience for me. Is the game worth $20? Absolutely not. If it seems like something you'd really enjoy, maybe spend $5-$10 on it. Maybe it will be improved upon in the future and be worth more, we'll see. I think the game has a decent foundation, so there is potential here. I'm also certainly not trying to take a dump on it as I have mad respect for solo developers. I hope things work out as I believe the game only recently hit 1.0

一次大胆将4X和打牌结合在一起的尝试 缺点还是在于平衡，不同资源之间的用处差别很大。核心问题在于城市的产出机制，文明6是一个城市有需要人口在地块上工作才能获得收益，而本作只需将有产出的地块纳入城市范围后自动就能获得收益，直接导致人口（食物）的作用急剧降低。虽然城市任然需要花费食物来扩张地块，然而地块的产出也仅在前期有点用，中期开始就基本不靠地块产出了。 反过来打牌（劳力）的收益是非常高的，城市改良需要用劳力建设，而一旦建设好无需人口能直接获得产出。更别提中期开始很多牌能直接开科技，然后一旦到了信息时代就可以无限回合了。直接导致这个游戏的最优解为：主要发展劳力，至少保证每回合能把手牌打空，然后用打牌给的改良和效果来发展科技。食物只需要有一点能保证改良有地方放就够了。 总结一下，大胆的4x + 卡牌的尝试，不过由于部分平衡问题导致策略深度并不算很深。仍然值得一玩，在初期有着不错的游戏体验

So I've almost got 100% of the achievements in this game, so it's fair to say I've played most of what this game has to offer. I was looking through the community tab to figure out a strategy to get a difficult achievement, and I saw a thread simply titled "AI slop" with the text inside saying "pay artists." After that was a very lengthy response from the developer venting about how difficult and frankly unprofitable it is for a solo dev to take on such an ambitious project. The dev claims 20% of the assets used AI tools. Frankly, I didn't even notice when I played that AI was involved. I would guess he didn't simply generate an asset and plop it in, he probably used it as a base and cleaned it up, but I'm not the dev so I didn't know. I find the extreme AI hate pretty sad tbh. AI can be used to make slop, or it can be used to make amazing art in the hands of a talented artist. In this case, I wouldn't say the visual art in this game is anything "amazing," but when you look at the game as a whole, the coding, the visuals, the audio, the game design, etc, it is a super impressive piece of art for an individual to make, even using AI tools. AI can facilitate genuinely good art. Look at the music video "Wave" by masaki mizuno, it's a super impressive use of AI tools. It's not just type in a prompt and generate. Corridor did a vfx breakdown of it and explained that they had to do a lot of work in blender to basically artistically direct what they wanted the generative AI to do. AI was merely a tool to facilitate a creative vision that required immense talent to execute. Check out the channel Neural Viz on youtube. They use AI as a tool to make their videos, but the videos a very well written and funny. This type of content would ordinarily only be produced by big budget studios who can afford to pay a lot of people to bring the vision to life, but now we can get a taste of content like that from individuals with time and dedication. Yes, 99%+ of AI content is garbage slop because garbage is super easy to generate. Likewise, how many crappy doodles are there compared to masterpiece drawings? A tool doesn't make art. An artist makes art using the tools at their disposal. This game is well made. There are no major bugs that make it unplayable.. The mechanics are fun. I feel like I got a complete game, nothing is unfinished. Let's not let the fact that a fraction of the assets used AI assistance detract from what is ultimately a solid and enjoyable game. Stop letting emotions dictate your thoughts.

"A Dream Concept with an Unbalanced Reality." As a massive Civilization fan, the pitch for Rogue Hex felt like it was made specifically for me. The idea of blending deep 4X strategy with deckbuilding and roguelike loops is a dream come true on paper, and initially, I was very optimistic about the loop. There is a clear spark of genius in the mechanics, but unfortunately, that excitement quickly faded as the game’s flaws began to overshadow its potential. The first major hurdle is the presentation. Visually, the game is quite difficult to look at. The art direction is a total mess, lacking any sense of cohesion or polish. Between the cluttered UI and the character designs—which I can only describe as hideous—the game feels like a collection of mismatched assets rather than a professional product. The "vibe" is just off, and while the music is passable at best, it does nothing to rescue the drab and uninviting atmosphere. The gameplay is where the most potential lies, but it is currently buried under a mountain of frustration. For a veteran strategy player, the barbarian system is particularly infuriating. They don’t just offer a challenge; they seem to exist outside the rules of the game, scaling at a rate that is consistently ahead of your own technology. This creates an experience that feels less like a fair roguelike "climb" and more like an unbalanced grind where you are punished regardless of your strategy. It is incredibly demoralizing to hit a brick wall every run because the enemies are fundamentally overtuned. I truly believe Rogue Hex shows promise. If the developer can commit to a major balancing overhaul and clean up the visual identity, this could be a standout title in the genre. However, in its current state, the frustration of the balancing and the lack of polish make it a hard pass. It’s a great idea that just isn’t ready for prime time yet.

Even worse, you cannot build units to counter them as you are dependent on the cards you are dealt. No matter how well you develop your science, they will always be at a higher level. Even if they are at the same level, they will always be stronger. A warrior cannot defeat a scout, for example. You cannot skip the tutorial and create a new game with parameters like few or no barbarians. The tutorial is the game. 20/100
